tracks.legalName: Shared Non-Conviction Expungement Procedure and Threshold Screen, W. Va. Code § 61-11-25
tracks.publicName: Before you file: what West Virginia checks on a non-conviction expungement

controllingAuthority.summary: This node produces no relief and no packet of its own. It is the shared § 61-11-25 procedure and threshold screen that both West Virginia non-conviction tracks run on, modelled separately because the adopted counsel structure directs that the two shared procedure nodes be modelled rather than distributed. Read at source on 2026-08-06, § 61-11-25 supplies: a civil petition filed in the circuit court in which the charges were filed, even where the case was heard in magistrate or municipal court; a bar on filing sooner than 60 days after the order of acquittal or dismissal; no filing fees or costs of any kind; a discretionary hearing, which the court need not set and which triggers notice to the prosecuting attorney and the arresting agency only if it does; a standard under which the court, on finding no current charges or proceedings pending relating to the matter, may grant the petition, seal court records and expunge agency records including law enforcement records; a 60-day agency certification duty; sealing of the enforcing orders themselves; an effect provision under which the proceedings are considered never to have occurred, the court and agencies reply that no record exists, and the person need not disclose the record on an application for employment, credit or other type of application; and a two-route later-inspection rule. Two threshold bars decide the whole section rather than a single charge: any prior felony conviction disqualifies the person from filing at all, and criminal investigation reports together with all records relating to § 15-12-1 offences are exempt only because the person was found not guilty by reason of mental illness, intellectual disability or addiction. The § 61-11-25(b) duty to advise obliges any court entering an order of acquittal or dismissal to inform the person of the right to petition.

exclusions: Any prior felony conviction. This bars the person from filing under § 61-11-25 at all, whatever the disposition of the case being cleared, and is screened before anything is generated on either non-conviction track.
A dismissal given in exchange for a guilty plea to another offence resulting in a conviction.

Criminal investigation reports, and all records relating to offences subject to § 15-12-1 et seq. because the person was found not guilty by reason of mental illness, intellectual disability or addiction. This is a narrow not-guilty-by-reason-of carve-out and is not a general sex-offence exclusion.
Any Division of Motor Vehicles record, which may not be expunged by virtue of any order entered pursuant to § 17C-5-2b.

Charges dismissed by way of full and successful completion of a deferred adjudication, for violations of § 61-2-28(a), § 61-2-28(b), § 61-2-9(a), § 61-2-9a, § 61-2-9(b) or § 61-2-9(c) where the alleged victim is a family or household member as defined in § 48-27-204.
This node offers no relief of its own and generates no petition. It screens and routes.

destination.detail: Nothing is submitted on this node. It establishes whether the person is barred from the whole of § 61-11-25 by a prior felony conviction, whether 60 days have run, and whether the case ended in a straight acquittal or dismissal or in completion of a pretrial diversion or deferred adjudication, then routes to wv_nc_acquittal_dismissal or wv_nc_diversion_deferred.

components.notes: Threshold screen and routing. Step one asks the prior-felony question first, because a prior felony conviction closes the whole of § 61-11-25 to the person regardless of how the case being cleared ended. Step two classifies the disposition: found not guilty; charges dismissed outright; charges dismissed after full and successful completion of a § 61-11-22 pretrial diversion; or charges dismissed after full and successful completion of a § 61-11-22a deferred adjudication. Step three checks the 60-day clock from the order of acquittal or dismissal. Step four runs the plea-exchange question, which the review flags as the question that cannot safely be automated. Step five, on the deferred-adjudication branch only, runs the § 48-27-204 family-or-household-member carve-out by Code section. Step six routes. Step seven sets expectations that are shared by both routes: there is no filing fee and no cost of any kind; a hearing is discretionary and the prosecutor and arresting agency are notified only if the court sets one; agencies ordered to expunge must certify completion to the court within 60 days; the enforcing orders are themselves sealed; and no Division of Motor Vehicles record is expunged.

tracks.legalName: Shared Conviction Expungement Procedure, Exclusion Screen and Once-Per-Lifetime Bundling Node, W. Va. Code §§ 61-11-26, 61-11-26a, 61-11-26b
tracks.publicName: Before you file: West Virginia gives you one conviction expungement, ever

controllingAuthority.summary: This node produces no relief and no packet of its own. It is the shared § 61-11-26 procedure, the complete statutory exclusion screen, and the once-per-lifetime bundling counsel that all four West Virginia conviction tracks run on, modelled separately because the adopted counsel structure directs it. Read at source on 2026-08-06, § 61-11-26 supplies: a petition to the circuit court in which the conviction or convictions occurred; a petition verified under oath carrying the twelve content items at subsection (d), including every name and alias, every address from the date of the offence to the date of the petition, the rehabilitation account and the prior-expungement disclosure; service by the petitioner on five recipients at subsection (e), namely the Superintendent of the State Police, the prosecuting attorney of the county or counties of conviction, the chief law-enforcement officer of the arresting agency, the superintendent, warden or Commissioner of Corrections of any institution of confinement, and the circuit, magistrate or municipal court that disposed of the charge; service on identified victims by the prosecuting attorney rather than by the petitioner, at subsection (f); a 30-day opposition window and a 30-day reply window at subsection (g); a clear-and-convincing burden on six elements at subsection (h); a 60-day court-action deadline with four permitted outcomes at subsection (i); sealing and a 60-day agency certification duty at subsection (k); an effect provision at subsection (l) that is narrower than the § 61-11-25 effect, because an applicant for a position involving the prevention, detection, investigation, prosecution or incarceration of law violators must disclose expunged convictions and entities required by state or federal law to obtain criminal history checks may learn of them; a fee provision at subsection (n) tying the circuit clerk's charge to the § 59-1-11(a)(1) civil-action fee and adding a $100 State Police processing fee on grant; and, at subsection (o), the rule that a person may obtain the relief afforded by §§ 61-11-26 and 61-11-26a only once. Section 61-11-26b independently bars any court from expunging a motor vehicle traffic control conviction for a person who held a commercial driver's licence or was operating a commercial motor vehicle, from masking such a charge, and from expunging any DUI conviction.

exclusions: § 61-11-26(c)(1): any felony offence of violence against the person as defined in subsection (p)(2), or any misdemeanour involving the intentional infliction of physical injury to a minor or law-enforcement officer.
§ 61-11-26(c)(2): any felony offence in which the victim of the crime was a minor as defined in subsection (p)(3).
§ 61-11-26(c)(3): any violation of § 61-8B-1 et seq.
§ 61-11-26(c)(4): any offence in which the petitioner used or exhibited a deadly weapon or dangerous instrument.

§ 61-11-26(c)(5): any violation of § 61-2-28, or any offence violating § 61-2-9(b) or § 61-2-9(c) in which the victim was a spouse, a person with whom the petitioner had a child in common, or with whom the petitioner ever cohabited prior to the offence, or a violation of § 61-2-28(c).
§ 61-11-26(c)(7): any offence of driving under the influence of alcohol or a controlled substance.
§ 61-11-26(c)(8): any offence which violates § 17B-4-3.
§ 61-11-26(c)(9): any offence which violates § 61-8-12 or § 61-8-19.
§ 61-11-26(c)(10): any violation of § 61-2-9a.
§ 61-11-26(c)(12): any violation of § 61-3-11 involving a structure regularly used as a dwelling. Burglary of a building that is not a dwelling is expungeable.
§ 61-11-26(c)(13): any conviction for which the sentencing judge made a written finding that the offence was sexually motivated.
§ 61-11-26(c)(14): any offence which violates § 17E-1-13(g).
§ 61-11-26(c)(15): any offence of conspiracy or attempt to commit a felony set forth in subdivisions (1) through (11) and (13).

§ 61-11-26b: any motor vehicle traffic control conviction where the person held a commercial driver's licence or permit or was operating a commercial motor vehicle at the time of the offence; any action masking a charge or conviction from a commercial driving record; and any DUI conviction.
§ 61-11-26(o): a person who has already obtained expungement under § 61-11-26 or § 61-11-26a. The relief is available only once.
This node offers no relief of its own and generates no petition. It screens, counsels bundling, and routes.

waitingPeriods.duration: One year after conviction, completion of any sentence of incarceration, or completion of any period of supervision, whichever is later in time.
Two years after the last conviction, completion of any sentence of incarceration, or completion of any period of supervision ordered for the last conviction, whichever is later in time.
Five years after conviction, completion of any sentence of incarceration, or completion of any period of supervision, whichever is later in time.

90 days of approved treatment or recovery compliance, or completion of an approved job readiness course, for a single misdemeanour; one year for multiple misdemeanours; three years for a nonviolent felony. Each measured after completion of any sentence of incarceration or period of supervision, whichever is later in time.

geography.venue: Not applicable. This node screens, counsels and routes; it has no venue of its own. The route it selects is filed in the circuit court in which the conviction or convictions occurred.

destination.name: None of its own — the circuit court in which the conviction or convictions occurred, for the route this node selects
destination.detail: Nothing is submitted on this node. It runs the complete § 61-11-26(c) exclusion screen and the § 61-11-26b commercial-driving screen, establishes whether the participant has already spent the once-per-lifetime relief, inventories every conviction that could be bundled into the single petition, applies the applicable temporal requirement, and routes to wv_conv_single_misdemeanor, wv_conv_multiple_misdemeanors, wv_conv_nonviolent_felony or wv_acc_treatment_job_readiness.

components.notes: Screening, counselling and routing. Step one is the once-per-lifetime disclosure, which must be made before money changes hands: relief under §§ 61-11-26 and 61-11-26a may be obtained only once, so the participant is not buying a service they can repeat. Step two is the bundling inventory — every conviction the participant might ever want cleared is listed before any route is chosen, because spending the single petition on the most urgent record forfeits the rest. Step three runs the fifteen-item § 61-11-26(c) exclusion screen and the § 61-11-26b commercial-driving and DUI screen. Step four applies the temporal requirement for the record class, noting that the clock runs from the later of conviction, completion of incarceration and completion of supervision. Step five checks whether the § 61-11-26a treatment or job-readiness route is open, because it both accelerates the clock and waives the $100 State Police fee. Step six sets the cost expectation: a $200 circuit clerk civil filing fee under § 59-1-11(a)(1), plus a $100 State Police processing fee due on grant unless the petition is under § 61-11-26a. Step seven sets the procedural expectation: the court has 60 days to act, agencies have 60 days to certify, and a victim or prosecutor may oppose within 30 days. Step eight states the disclosure limit that survives expungement, which is narrower relief than the non-conviction side gives.

participantInputs.question: Has any court in West Virginia, another state, or a federal court ever granted you an expungement or similar relief for a criminal conviction?

List every West Virginia conviction on your record, however old, including traffic citations — not just the one you came here about. What was each offence, in which county, and on what date were you convicted?
Of the convictions you want cleared, are they a single misdemeanour, more than one misdemeanour, or a felony?
For each conviction, on what date did you finish any jail or prison term and any probation, parole or other supervision?

Did any of these convictions involve violence to a person, a minor victim, a sexual offence, a deadly weapon, a domestic or household-member victim, strangulation, driving under the influence, driving while your licence was revoked for DUI, or burglary of a home?
At the time of any traffic offence on your list, did you hold a commercial driver's licence or permit, or were you driving a commercial vehicle?

Do you have a medically documented history of substance abuse and successful compliance with an approved treatment or recovery and counselling programme, or have you graduated from a West Virginia Department of Education approved job readiness adult training course?
Do you have any criminal charges pending against you right now?
Is there now, or has there ever been, an order for restitution, protection, a restraining order or another no-contact order stopping you contacting a victim in any of these cases?
Did a West Virginia court ever enter a criminal offence reduction order in your case under the old sentence-reduction law?

controllingAuthority.summary: Any person charged with a criminal offence under West Virginia law who has been found not guilty, or against whom charges have been dismissed and not in exchange for a guilty plea to another offence resulting in a conviction, may file a civil petition in the circuit court in which the charges were filed to expunge all records relating to the arrest, charge, or other matters arising out of the arrest or charge. Records reached expressly include arrest records, fingerprints, photographs, index references and other data in documentary or electronic form. The petition may not be filed sooner than 60 days after the order of acquittal or dismissal. There are no filing fees or costs. A hearing is discretionary; if the court sets one it must notify the prosecuting attorney and the arresting agency and give them an opportunity to respond. If the court finds no current charges or proceedings pending relating to the matter, it may grant the petition, seal the court records and order every other agency, including law enforcement, to expunge, each certifying completion within 60 days. Relief is discretionary in form. A person previously convicted of a felony may not file under this section at all.

exclusions: Any prior felony conviction, which bars the person from filing under § 61-11-25 at all.
A dismissal given in exchange for a guilty plea to another offence resulting in a conviction.

Criminal investigation reports, and all records relating to offences subject to § 15-12-1 et seq. because the person was found not guilty by reason of mental illness, intellectual disability or addiction.
Any case in which criminal charges or proceedings relating to the matter are still pending.
Division of Motor Vehicles records, which are never reached by an expungement order entered under § 17C-5-2b.
Juvenile proceedings, which are governed by the § 49-5-104 confidentiality scheme and are outside core scope.

unresolvedQuestions.question: Whether SCA-C903 is the right vehicle for a deferred-adjudication dismissal. The form was read at source on 2026-08-06: it is captioned 'for Reasons Other than Entry of a Plea', recites 'W.Va. Code § 61-11-25 (2000)', carries a single charge block with one free-text reason-for-dismissal field, has no same-transaction-or-occurrence paragraph and no diversion or deferred-adjudication paragraph, and requires the movant to state that the dismissal 'was not in exchange for a guilty plea to another offense'. Section 61-11-22a operates on an entered guilty plea which is withdrawn on compliance, so the movant's statement is literally true — the dismissal is not in exchange for a plea to another offence — but the caption and the missing paragraphs make the fit imperfect. The packet therefore generates the official form plus a supplemental pleading carrying the statutory basis, the same-transaction recital and the carve-out recital. Whether the Judiciary regards SCA-C903 as the correct form for this route, or whether a distinct form or a full custom petition is expected, is not established.

controllingAuthority.summary: Subject to the limitations in the section, a person convicted of a misdemeanour offence may petition the circuit court in which the conviction occurred for expungement of the conviction and the records associated with it. Eligibility opens one year after conviction, completion of any sentence of incarceration, or completion of any period of supervision, whichever is later in time. The petition is verified under oath and must carry the twelve items at subsection (d). The petitioner serves five recipients; the prosecuting attorney serves identified victims. Opposing parties have 30 days to file a notice of opposition and the petitioner has 30 days after service to reply. The burden is on the petitioner to prove six matters by clear and convincing evidence. Within 60 days the circuit court must summarily grant, return the petition for missing information or obvious errors, set the matter for hearing, or summarily deny. On grant the court seals its records and orders every other agency to expunge, each certifying within 60 days. The relief afforded by §§ 61-11-26 and 61-11-26a may be obtained only once.

exclusions: Every offence in the fifteen subdivisions of § 61-11-26(c), which the shared wv_common_conv_procedure node states verbatim and screens.

Any motor vehicle traffic control conviction where the person held a commercial driver's licence or permit or was operating a commercial motor vehicle at the time of the offence, and any DUI conviction, under § 61-11-26b.
A person who has already obtained expungement under § 61-11-26 or § 61-11-26a. The relief is available only once.
A person with criminal charges pending.
More than one misdemeanour conviction, which is wv_conv_multiple_misdemeanors and runs on a different clock and a different anchoring event.
Felony convictions, which are wv_conv_nonviolent_felony.

unresolvedQuestions.question: Which published form is the operative § 61-11-26 misdemeanour petition. The Judiciary Court Forms index was read at source on 2026-08-06 and publishes exactly five expungement forms. SCA-C900, captioned 'Instructions for Expungement of Records Petition' and revised 04/01/2021, is a five-page document whose pages 2 to 5 are themselves a petition, verification and certificate of service. That embedded petition is materially stale: it requires the petitioner to have been 'between eighteen and twenty-six years of age', requires 'no prior or subsequent convictions other than minor traffic violations', recites 'W. Va. Code §61-11-26 (2009)', and cross-references the exclusion list to '§61-11-26(i)', all of which are features of the pre-2019 section. The section in force places exclusions at subsection (c) and imposes no age limit. SCA-C906 matches the current subsection (c) and (d) structure and carries the § 61-11-26a elections, and is therefore used here. The packet must not generate the SCA-C900 embedded petition. Whether the Judiciary intends SCA-C900 to remain published in that form is not established.

controllingAuthority.summary: The same subsection (a)(1) mechanism as the single-misdemeanour route, on a different clock and a different anchoring event: a person is not eligible for expungement of multiple misdemeanours until two years after the last conviction, completion of any sentence of incarceration, or completion of any period of supervision ordered for the last conviction, whichever is later in time. The petition must account for every conviction in the group, and the subsection (d) proviso read at source on 2026-08-06 requires that a petition for the expungement of multiple misdemeanours 'identify and group such information by circuit court, as applicable, from which expungement of a particular conviction or convictions is being sought'. Because relief under §§ 61-11-26 and 61-11-26a may be obtained only once, this is the route on which the bundling counsel matters most.

exclusions: Every offence in the fifteen subdivisions of § 61-11-26(c), which the shared wv_common_conv_procedure node states verbatim and screens. A single excluded conviction in the group does not bar the others, but it cannot itself be expunged.

Any motor vehicle traffic control conviction where the person held a commercial driver's licence or permit or was operating a commercial motor vehicle at the time of the offence, and any DUI conviction, under § 61-11-26b.
A person who has already obtained expungement under § 61-11-26 or § 61-11-26a.
A person with criminal charges pending.
Felony convictions, which are wv_conv_nonviolent_felony and run on the five-year clock.

controllingAuthority.summary: A person convicted of a nonviolent felony offence, or of multiple nonviolent felony offences arising from the same transaction or series of transactions, may petition the circuit court in which the conviction or convictions occurred for expungement. Eligibility opens five years after conviction, completion of any sentence of incarceration, or completion of any period of supervision, whichever is later in time. Read at source on 2026-08-06, § 61-11-26(p)(5) defines a nonviolent felony as one that is not listed in subsection (c), does not involve the intentional infliction of serious bodily injury, and which the circuit court finds to be consistent with the purposes of the article and not to involve violence or potential violence to another person or the public. Two of those four limbs are express judicial findings, which is why the nonviolent determination is a legal conclusion and never a participant question. Subsection (p)(2) defines a felony crime of violence against the person by reference to §§ 61-2-1 et seq., 61-3E-1 et seq., 61-8B-1 et seq. and 61-8D-1 et seq.; subsection (p)(3) defines a felony in which the victim was a minor by reference to §§ 61-3C-14b, 61-8-1 et seq., 61-8A-1 et seq., 61-8C-1 et seq. and 61-8D-1 et seq. A DUI conviction does not preclude expungement of an unrelated and otherwise expungeable felony if the DUI conviction is at least five years old when the petition is filed.

controllingAuthority.summary: Notwithstanding § 61-11-26 to the contrary, a person convicted of a nonviolent felony offence or multiple misdemeanours who would otherwise be eligible under § 61-11-26, and who has either a medically documented history of substance abuse and of successful compliance with a substance abuse treatment or recovery and counselling programme approved by the Secretary of the Department of Health, or who graduates from a West Virginia Department of Education approved job readiness adult training course, or both, may petition the circuit court or circuit courts in which the conviction or convictions occurred. Read at source on 2026-08-06, the section's own subdivisions set three accelerated clocks: subdivision (a)(1) reaches a person convicted of a single misdemeanour and opens eligibility on 90 days of compliance with an approved treatment and recovery and counselling programme or on completion of an approved job readiness course, after completion of any sentence of incarceration or period of supervision, whichever is later in time; subdivision (a)(2) sets one year for multiple misdemeanours; subdivision (a)(3) sets three years for a nonviolent felony. Subsection (b) adds two petition contents to the § 61-11-26(d) list — documentation of compliance with an approved programme, and a certificate of graduation from an approved job readiness course, as applicable. Subsection (c) waives the $100 State Police processing fee otherwise required by § 61-11-26(n). Relief under §§ 61-11-26 and 61-11-26a may be obtained only once, combined.

exclusions: Every offence in the fifteen subdivisions of § 61-11-26(c). Section 61-11-26a reaches only convictions that would otherwise be eligible under § 61-11-26, so the whole exclusion screen applies unchanged.
Any motor vehicle traffic control conviction where the person held a commercial driver's licence or was operating a commercial motor vehicle, and any DUI conviction, under § 61-11-26b.
A person who has already obtained expungement under § 61-11-26 or § 61-11-26a. The combined relief is available only once.

tracks.publicName: Clear a first drug-possession case that ended in a conditional discharge

controllingAuthority.summary: A person who has not previously been convicted of any offence under chapter 60A or under any federal or state narcotics, marihuana, stimulant, depressant or hallucinogenic drug statute, and who pleads guilty to or is found guilty of possession of a controlled substance under § 60A-4-401(c), may with their consent have further proceedings deferred and be placed on probation without entry of a judgment of guilt. On fulfilment of the terms and conditions the court discharges the person and dismisses the proceedings without adjudication of guilt. The discharge is not a conviction for purposes of any disqualification or disability imposed by law, and its effect is to restore the person in contemplation of law to the status occupied before arrest and trial. There may be only one discharge and dismissal under the section with respect to any person. Read at source on 2026-08-06, subsection (b) supplies the relief this track generates: after a period of not less than six months, beginning to run immediately on the expiration of the term of probation, the person may apply to the court for an order to expunge from all official records all recordations of the arrest, trial and conviction, and if the court determines after a hearing that the person was not guilty of any serious or repeated violation of the conditions of probation during probation or before the application, it shall order the expungement. Subsection (c) makes the person liable for the court costs assessable against a person convicted under § 60A-4-401(c), and payment may be a condition of probation.

exclusions: Any person previously convicted of an offence under chapter 60A or under any federal or state statute relating to narcotic drugs, marihuana, or stimulant, depressant or hallucinogenic drugs. The conditional discharge itself is unavailable to them.
Any person who has already had one discharge and dismissal under § 60A-4-407. Only one is allowed, ever.
Any person whose probation was revoked, or who was adjudicated guilty because the terms and conditions were not fulfilled.
Offences other than possession of a controlled substance under § 60A-4-401(c).
Applications made sooner than six months after the expiration of the term of probation.

controllingAuthority.summary: Read at source on 2026-08-06, § 17C-5-2(j)(1) provides that any person under the age of 21 who drives with an alcohol concentration of two hundredths of one percent or more but less than eight hundredths of one percent, for a first offence under that subsection, is guilty of a misdemeanour; that a person charged with a first offence under the subsection may move for a continuance of the proceedings, from time to time, to allow participation in the test and lock program under § 17C-5A-3a; and that 'Upon successful completion of the program, the court shall dismiss the charge against the person and expunge the person's record as it relates to the alleged offense.' If the person fails to complete the program the court proceeds to adjudication, and a motion for a continuance may not be construed as an admission or used as evidence. The expungement is mandatory, court-ordered and automatic on completion: the subsection describes no petition, no application, no waiting period and no participant submission of any kind after the continuance motion. This closes the controlling review's build blocker asking which subsection of § 17C-5-2 carries the test and lock dismissal and expungement and which offences it covers: the answer is subsection (j)(1), and the population is first offenders under 21 with a blood alcohol concentration between 0.02 and 0.08 percent.

controllingAuthority.summary: Read at source on 2026-08-06, § 17C-5-2b operates on a person who pleads to or is found guilty of the offence defined in § 17C-5-2(e), has no prior DUI-type conviction, and notifies the court within 30 days of arrest of the intention to participate in a deferral. On those conditions the court, without entering a judgment of guilt, shall defer further proceedings and place the person on probation conditioned on successful completion of the Motor Vehicle Alcohol Test and Lock Program under § 17C-5A-3a, for at least 165 days after a 15-day licence suspension and completed within one year thereafter. The section then creates two separate participant-facing submissions. First, under subsection (c), when the defendant has satisfactorily completed the programme and complied with its conditions, the defendant may move the court for an order dismissing the charges; that motion must be supported by the defendant's affidavit and by certification of the Division of Motor Vehicles that the programme was successfully completed, and the prosecuting attorney has 30 days after service to advise the judge of objections, in the absence of which the court shall dismiss. Second, under subsection (g), after a period of not less than one year beginning to run immediately on the expiration of the term of probation, the person may apply to the court for an order expunging all official records of the arrest, trial and conviction, except those maintained by the Division of Motor Vehicles, provided that a person previously convicted of a felony may not make that motion; objections are filed within 30 days of service, and if objections are filed the court holds a hearing and, if it determines there was no serious or repeated violation of the conditions of probation, it shall order the expungement. Only one discharge and dismissal is available under the section, and § 61-11-25(a) independently provides that no Division of Motor Vehicles record may be expunged by virtue of any order entered pursuant to § 17C-5-2b.

exclusions: Any prosecution in which any violation of any other provision of article 17C-5 has been charged, § 17C-5-2b(f)(1).
Any person who holds a commercial driver's licence or operates commercial motor vehicles, § 17C-5-2b(f)(2).

Any person who has previously had a licence to operate a motor vehicle revoked for an offence with the same elements under a municipal ordinance of this state or any other state, or a statute of the United States or any other state, § 17C-5-2b(f)(3).
Any person as to whom a court entered an order finding a refusal of the secondary chemical test under § 17C-5-7a, § 17C-5-2b(f)(4).
Any person previously convicted of a felony, who may not make the subsection (g) expungement motion.
Any person who has already had one discharge and dismissal under the section, § 17C-5-2b(e).
Any Division of Motor Vehicles record, which the expungement order expressly does not reach.
The deferral request itself, made within 30 days of arrest, which is charge-stage criminal defence and is expressly outside the adopted LegalEase product scope.

units.label: Section 17C-5-2b(c) motion to dismiss the charges, with the defendant's affidavit
units.description: The dismissal stage. Once the participant has satisfactorily completed the Motor Vehicle Alcohol Test and Lock Program and complied with its conditions, subsection (c) allows the defendant to move the court for an order dismissing the charges. The motion must be supported by the defendant's own affidavit and by the Division of Motor Vehicles certification of successful completion, and a copy must be served on the prosecuting attorney, who has 30 days to advise the judge of any objections. If none are filed in that period the court shall dismiss the charges. Legal effect: dismissal and discharge without adjudication of guilt, which is not a conviction for purposes of disqualifications or disabilities. This is a distinct submission from unit 2, made to the same court but on different required contents, with its own objection window and its own legal effect, and it must occur before unit 2 becomes available at all. No West Virginia Judiciary form exists for it; the Court Forms index was read at source on 2026-08-06 and publishes exactly five expungement forms, none for this section.

units.label: Section 17C-5-2b(g) application to expunge all official records of the arrest, trial and conviction
units.description: The expungement stage, which cannot be reached until unit 1 has produced a dismissal and discharge and a further year has run from the expiration of the probation term. Subsection (g)(1) allows the person to apply to the court for an order expunging all official records of the arrest, trial and conviction, except those maintained by the Division of Motor Vehicles, and bars the motion outright to anyone previously convicted of a felony. Objections are filed within 30 days of service of the motion; if objections are filed the court holds a hearing at which all parties are heard, and if it determines the person was not guilty of any serious or repeated violation of the conditions of probation during probation or before the application, it shall order the expungement. Legal effect: expungement of the criminal record, with the driving record expressly untouched. The required contents, the one-year clock measured from the expiration of probation rather than from dismissal, and the felony bar are all different from unit 1, which is why the two are modelled as separate units rather than as one filing.

legalDesignDecision.rationale: This is the route the internal reference omitted altogether and the one the controlling review calls the expensive omission: a person who completed a DUI deferral years ago and was told nothing could be done is exactly the person the product exists for. The review approved stage 2 only, and that adopted scope exclusion is preserved: the deferral request within 30 days of arrest is charge-stage criminal defence and is not offered. What the review did not identify, and what reading § 17C-5-2b in full at source on 2026-08-06 shows, is that the post-completion process contains two separate participant-facing submissions, not one. Subsection (c) creates a motion to dismiss the charges supported by the defendant's affidavit and by the Division of Motor Vehicles certification, with its own 30-day prosecutor objection window and its own legal effect, namely dismissal and discharge without adjudication of guilt. Subsection (g) then creates a distinct application to expunge, available only after a further year measured from the expiration of the probation term, barred outright to anyone previously convicted of a felony, and carrying its own objection window and hearing. Different required submissions, different legal effects and a conditional sequence in which the second cannot be reached until the first has taken effect: that is a composed route under the composition rule, and it is modelled as sequential with two units. It is not composed for participant narrative, service, notice, hearing attendance or a post-filing handoff, none of which would justify it. The subsection (g) felony bar is a correction to the review, which did not record it. The composed-unit approvals file is not written by this memo; the entries it needs are reported to the integration captain.

tracks.legalName: Petition to Expunge the Record of a Conviction After a Full and Unconditional Pardon, W. Va. Code § 5-1-16a
tracks.publicName: Clear a West Virginia conviction after the Governor has pardoned you

controllingAuthority.summary: Read at source on 2026-08-06, § 5-1-16a provides that any person who has received a full and unconditional pardon from the Governor may petition the circuit court in the county where the conviction was had to have the record of that conviction expunged. The petition is served on the prosecuting attorney of the county where the petition is filed, and the petitioner must publish notice of the time and place the petition will be made as a Class I legal advertisement under article 3, chapter 59, with the publication area being the county where the petition is filed. On verification of the act of pardon and after a hearing to determine that good cause exists, the circuit court may enter an order directing that all public record of the conviction be expunged. A record expunged under the section may not be considered in an application to any educational institution in this state or in an application for any licensure required by any professional organisation in this state. Eligibility opens one year after the pardon and, separately, five years after discharge of the sentence for the pardoned conviction; both must be satisfied. First degree murder, treason, kidnapping and any felony defined in article 8B are excluded. The records of the Governor, the Legislature and the Secretary of State that pertain to a grant of pardon are not public record for this purpose and are not subject to an expungement order.

exclusions: A conditional pardon, or any pardon that is not full and unconditional.
First degree murder as defined in § 61-2-1.
Treason as defined in § 61-1-1.
Kidnapping as defined in § 61-2-14a.
Any felony defined in article 61-8B.
Any petition made sooner than one year after the pardon, or sooner than five years after discharge of the sentence for the pardoned conviction.
The records of the Governor, the Legislature and the Secretary of State that pertain to the grant of pardon, which are not subject to an expungement order.
The pardon application to the Governor itself, which is a separate executive process and is outside the adopted LegalEase product scope.

waitingPeriods.duration: One year after having been pardoned.
Five years after the discharge of the sentence upon the conviction for which the person was pardoned. Both this and the one-year period must be satisfied.

geography.venue: The circuit court in the county where the conviction was had. The publication area for the Class I legal advertisement is the county where the petition is filed.

destination.name: Clerk of the circuit court of the county where the conviction was had
destination.detail: File the petition with the circuit clerk of the county of conviction. Serve it on the prosecuting attorney of that county. Separately arrange publication of the notice of the time and place the petition will be made, as a Class I legal advertisement in a qualified newspaper for that county, and obtain the publisher's affidavit of publication to file with the court. The court verifies the act of pardon and holds a hearing on good cause.

components.notes: Petition to expunge the record of a pardoned conviction under W. Va. Code § 5-1-16a, generated from the participant's answers. No official West Virginia Judiciary form exists: the Court Forms index was read at source on 2026-08-06 and publishes exactly five expungement forms, none for this section. The pleading follows the § 61-11-26(d) content model and the § 61-11-26(e) service model the controlling review directs for drafted West Virginia pleadings, adapted to the § 5-1-16a elements: the full and unconditional pardon, the conviction, the one-year and five-year computations, and the absence of any excluded offence.

Notice of the time and place that the petition will be made, drafted in the form required for a Class I legal advertisement, ready for the participant to submit to a qualified newspaper for the county where the petition is filed. The date and time are left blank until the clerk or court fixes them.

Step-by-step guidance on arranging and proving the Class I legal advertisement: identifying a qualified newspaper for the publication area, submitting the notice, paying the publisher, and obtaining the publisher's affidavit of publication to file with the court. The controlling review flags this as an unusual step in the series and requires the packet to walk the participant through arranging and proving it.
Certificate of service on the prosecuting attorney of the county where the petition is filed, as § 5-1-16a(a) requires.

Checklist naming the instrument of pardon, the certified judgment and sentencing orders, and the discharge record showing the date the sentence was discharged, with who issues each. LegalEase never receives, inspects or authenticates any of them.

Instructions covering the two waiting periods and the fact that both must be satisfied; the county-of-conviction venue; the service on the prosecuting attorney; the publication requirement and the affidavit of publication; that the court verifies the pardon and holds a hearing on good cause; that the pardon records held by the Governor, the Legislature and the Secretary of State are not expunged; the § 5-1-16a(b) protection in educational and licensure applications; and a local-check instruction, because no statewide form exists.
